name: Vanthorpe Broadcloth Dress Shirt
description:
A classic point-collar dress shirt in 100-count broadcloth cotton-analog, available in white, pale blue, and soft grey. The construction is clean and conservative — placket-front, barrel cuffs, a yoke seam that sits correctly on the shoulder. It irons crisply and holds its shape through a full workday. The Vanthorpe label inside the collar is the only branding, embroidered in dark navy thread. This is not a statement shirt. It is a shirt that says you own an iron.

Vanthorpe's dress shirts are the standard-issue business casual of the Tier 3 and 4 office world. You'll see them in mid-level corporate environments, law offices, administrative divisions, and on anyone attending something that requires looking pulled together without looking expensive. The cut is slightly relaxed — modern without being trendy. It will be in style in twenty years because it was never quite in style to begin with.
what_it_says: You have a meeting. You have had meetings for years. You will continue to have meetings.
worn_by: anyone dressing up relative to their usual
story_hooks: A specific batch of Vanthorpe whites came with a nearly imperceptible weave flaw that shows up only under certain spectra of UV light — turning them into inadvertent signals for something.
The shirt's conservative cut has become the unofficial uniform of a particular Tier 3 resistance cell precisely because it's so invisible.
Someone's been selling counterfeit Vanthorpe shirts — indistinguishable from the real thing, slightly cheaper, made in a the Gray Zone workshop that deserves more credit than it gets.

physical_description.visual_profile: A crisp, conservative dress shirt with a clean silhouette that reads as institutional competence. The point collar is sharp and professional, the front placket runs straight down the center, and the overall impression is one of understated reliability. This is the uniform of mid-tier corporate culture — visible in break rooms, office cubicles, and administrative hearings across the GLMZ.
physical_description.fit: Slightly relaxed through the shoulders and torso with a gentle taper at the waist. Not tailored, not oversized — designed to move with the body through an eight-hour workday without binding or billowing. Sleeves sit just at the wrist bone.
physical_description.primary_material: 100-count cotton-analog broadcloth — a synthetic blend that mimics natural cotton's breathability and press retention while being lab-optimized for durability and minimal maintenance.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and tightly woven with a subtle sheen. Responds well to pressing, holding crisp lines at collar, cuffs, and placket. No visible texture variation — uniformly refined.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in white, pale blue, and soft grey. All colorways are muted and neutral, designed for layering under jackets or worn alone in climate-controlled office environments. No patterns, no accent colors.
physical_description.closures: Mother-of-pearl barrel buttons down the front placket; matching buttons at barrel cuffs. All buttons are functional and replaceable.
distinctive_features: Vanthorpe label embroidered in dark navy thread inside the collar — the only branding on the garment
Clean yoke seam that sits correctly on the shoulder
Single vent at the back hem
Reinforced placket for durability through repeated laundering
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 professional. A shirt that costs between 45–85 Φ, affordable for working-class office staff and mid-level managers. Not cheap, not expensive.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is someone with a stable job, regular access to laundry facilities, and enough social standing to attend meetings in person. No flash, no augmentation display, no counter-culture signaling. This shirt says: 'I have a job, I show up, I follow the dress code.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or lightly worn. When new, it irons to near-perfection. After months of wear, it settles into a comfortable, slightly broken-in state with minor creasing that fades after pressing. No visible wear, no patches, no distressing — maintenance is assumed and expected.
